solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Food, something in freezer on right (4)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B

blocks.note: ice is what a freezer makes

annotation.surface: Someone pointing out where the food sits in the freezer.
annotation.walkthrough: The ICE is written after the R, which is what 'on' asks for in an across answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the grain is one of the world's staple foods, so 'Food' names the class it belongs to.

entries.clue: Boost has excited archer, eg (8)

indicatorNotes.excited: stirred up, so the letters are thrown about

annotation.surface: An archer, say, gets a lift from excitement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'eg' looks like it introduces an example, but its two letters are part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by metaphor: topping up a flat battery is the image behind giving someone's energy a boost.

entries.clue: Tea bags in tea cups etc (5)

indicatorNotes.bags: to bag is to hold inside, so CHA holds IN

blocks.note: used as it stands, placed inside CH…A

annotation.surface: Tea bags sitting in the cups ready for brewing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tea bags' reads as the thing you dunk; here 'bags' is a verb and 'Tea' is CHA holding IN.
annotation.definitionFit: A collective noun: the word covers cups, saucers and plates made of porcelain, and 'etc' admits the rest of the set.

entries.clue: Piano, scratched on the outside, thrown on rubbish tip (8)

indicatorNotes.on the outside: SCRAPED sits outside P, wrapping it

annotation.surface: A battered piano, scratched all over, is dumped at the tip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piano' looks like the thing being dumped, but it is just the musical abbreviation; the extra P is why the answer has a double letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something junked as worthless ends up at the tip, and the adjective matches the past participle 'thrown'.

entries.clue: New topic on mental thought (13)

indicatorNotes.New: a new form of the letters: they are rearranged

annotation.surface: A fresh subject about mental thinking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'on' reads as a preposition but its letters belong in the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the noun 'thought' in its sense of quiet reflection, as in 'lost in thought'.

entries.clue: Overturned sheet on which is a pseudonym (5)

indicatorNotes.Overturned: turned upside down: in a down answer, read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.on which is: in a down answer, what sits on top comes first

blocks.note: a sheet is a sail, and sail turned over is LIAS

annotation.surface: A capsized boat's sail, with someone's false name painted on it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sheet' suggests bedding or paper; on a boat a sheet is also a sail, the sense used here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name an assumed name used in place of your real one.

entries.clue: Paul ate off table (7)

indicatorNotes.off: gone bad, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

annotation.surface: Paul, eating straight off the table without a plate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'table' reads as furniture, but it is tableland: a flat-topped high plain.
annotation.definitionFit: A geographical sense: 'table' or tableland is raised ground with a flat top, like Table Mountain.

entries.clue: Go out as part of crowd at event (4)

indicatorNotes.as part of: the answer forms only a part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'crowd', through 'at', into the start of 'event'

annotation.surface: Slipping out of a party while mingling with the crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: crowD AT Event: the answer bridges three words.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to go out with someone is to be romantically seeing them, so the verbs match.

entries.clue: The law reforms in plentiful supply (6)

indicatorNotes.reforms: forms again: the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Legal reforms arriving in abundance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'reforms' looks like a noun in a news headline; here it is a verb telling THE LAW to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A secondary sense: beyond riches, the word means an abundance, as in 'a wealth of detail'.

entries.clue: Greek character accompanied by slim South American (7)

blocks.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

annotation.surface: A Greek person travelling with a thin South American companion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person from Greece; in crosswords it is usually a letter of the alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a person from Chile is one kind of South American.

entries.clue: Coloured paint unsuitable (5)

indicatorNotes.Coloured: coloured means distorted or altered, so the letters change

annotation.surface: A decorator rejecting a coloured paint as the wrong shade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coloured' fits paint so naturally that it hides its job: as in 'coloured by prejudice', it means distorted.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the negative prefix on 'apt' (fitting) gives an adjective meaning not fitting.

entries.clue: Ever a grown-up? (2,3)

blocks.note: a grown-up child has grown tall

annotation.surface: A wistful question: was I ever really an adult?
annotation.walkthrough: 'grown-up' reads as a noun, an adult; it is taken as an adjective, grown up tall.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: in questions and negatives the two are interchangeable, as in 'did you ever doubt it?'

entries.clue: Consumer embraces beginning of song festival (6)

indicatorNotes.embraces: EATER holds the S in its arms

annotation.surface: A shopper swept up in a song festival.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Consumer' suggests a shopper; here it is someone who consumes food.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the spring Christian feast of the resurrection is one festival among many.

entries.clue: Loose as it were, most ready to drop (8)

indicatorNotes.Loose: the letters are set loose and re-form

annotation.surface: Something hanging loose, on the point of falling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'ready to drop' pairs with 'Loose' to suggest a falling object; it means exhausted.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'ready to drop' is dead tired, and the superlative matches 'most'.

entries.clue: Succeed as paparazzo — see? (3,3,7)

blocks.note: a paparazzo succeeds by landing the photo

annotation.surface: A celebrity photographer landing the shot, and asking if you follow.
annotation.walkthrough: A paparazzo is a photographer who chases celebrities. 'see?' is the everyday 'understand?', not looking.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: literally, a photographer securing the shot; as an idiom, grasping the situation, which is what 'see?' asks.

entries.clue: Bit of a daffy instrument! (7)

blocks.note: the frilled central tube of a daffodil, short here to 'daffy'

annotation.surface: A slightly silly musical instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'daffy' means silly, but here it is short for daffodil, whose frilled centre is named after the brass instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the brass instrument, and the flared corona of a daffodil, which is shaped like its bell.

entries.clue: Critical moment, sound of teeth on Corn Flakes? (6)

annotation.definition2: sound of teeth on Corn Flakes

blocks.note: the decisive point when a matter comes to a head

blocks.clueFragment: sound of teeth on Corn Flakes
blocks.note: the noise of biting dry cereal

annotation.surface: A tense moment at breakfast, spoon poised over the cereal.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half needs no trick: it simply describes the noise, and the phrase 'when it comes to the crunch' gives the first.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: an idiom for the decisive moment, and the imitative word for biting something brittle.

entries.clue: Two articles written by chap in country (6)

indicatorNotes.written by: set beside, so the articles follow GUY

blocks.note: the indefinite articles AN and A

annotation.surface: A man who wrote a pair of newspaper pieces while abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests newspaper pieces; it means the grammatical articles A and AN.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the former British colony on South America's north coast is one country among many.

entries.clue: Letter a prickly thing? (5)

blocks.note: an itch is a prickling feeling

annotation.surface: A letter described as a prickly thing, like a thorny note.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is how the letter H is spelt out in full.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is the spelt-out name of H, one letter of the alphabet.

entries.clue: Blade losing its edge, say (5)

indicatorNotes.losing its edge: a word's edge is its outermost letter, here the front one

blocks.note: the first letter C is dropped

annotation.surface: A knife that has gone blunt, so to speak.
annotation.walkthrough: 'losing its edge' fits a blade going blunt; here the edge is the first letter C.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to speak words aloud, as in 'she didn't say a word'.

entries.clue: Performer in gutter, one tanked up (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the letters are inside the following words
indicatorNotes.up: in a down answer, going up means reading backwards

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of 'gutter', all of 'one' and the start of 'tanked'; 'up' then reverses them

annotation.surface: A drunken busker lying in the gutter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'tanked up' reads as drunk, but 'up' is detached to reverse the hidden letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a singer in the high male voice range is one kind of performer.

entries.clue: Head scratched in difficult argument (4)

indicatorNotes.Head scratched: to scratch is to strike out, and the head is the first letter

blocks.note: stiff = difficult, as a stiff test
the first letter S is dropped

annotation.surface: Someone scratching their head during a tricky argument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head scratched' is a puzzled gesture; here it means the front letter is removed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, narrowed: a petty quarrel between people close to each other is a small argument.

entries.clue: Popular place for contribution (5)

annotation.surface: A popular venue asking for donations.
annotation.walkthrough: 'place' reads as a noun, a venue; it is the verb, to put.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what someone adds to a discussion or project, as in 'thanks for your contribution'.

entries.clue: Perfume in smell, might you say? (7)

indicatorNotes.might you say: points to how the phrase would be spoken

blocks.note: a smell is a scent, so 'in smell' becomes 'in scents'

annotation.surface: Wondering whether a perfume is really just a nice smell.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue asks you to translate 'smell' before speaking it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word means both fragrant smoke and, more loosely, any sweet perfume.

entries.clue: Lovely dog’s activity? (8)

blocks.note: dogs bring back thrown sticks and balls

annotation.surface: A lovely dog at play.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second definition as an example: bringing back a ball is one thing dogs do.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjective for attractive, and the present participle of the verb for retrieving a thrown stick.

entries.clue: Brood in ferment at regular intervals (4)

indicatorNotes.at regular intervals: letters taken at evenly spaced gaps: here every second one, starting with the first

annotation.surface: Stewing over something while agitated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'ferment' tempts as a synonym for brood; it only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to dwell anxiously on a worry.
